Why can't I see the camera's reflection?

  • A tilt/shift lens - just keep a camera parallel to the mirrored area, but off to the side, and then shift the lens sideways toward the mirror, the picture will appear as if taken head-on. Makes for the Vampire effect
  • A longer focal length lens and place yourself further away - making yourself less conspicuous. Especially since you'll notice that there is a vertical displacement of the building due to the concrete foundation.
  • Photoshop

I'm intelligent and a hard worker, but I have this increasingly apparent issue with little stuff. I'm talking about mistakes like misplacing things, procrastinating, disorganization, not listening fully to directions, not checking things thoroughly, and so on. Stuff that doesn't seem like a big deal on its own but can end up causing real problems. The most recent example is missing a flight yesterday because I failed to account for the time zone change caused by my previous flight. I could have easily just checked the time after we landed - I was even sitting next to someone who was talking about how little time she had before her next flight - but I just assumed I was okay and that I still had about an hour before boarding. This is only one of many instances of my brain farts. And because this is such a broad flaw, it's difficult to fix. Has anyone else struggled with this and done anything about it?
I consistently screw up the little things in my daily life

One of my coping strategies is to leave early for things. I know it only takes me 5 minutes(actually timed) to get between buildings where I work. I leave for meetings 15 minutes ahead of time. Sounds trivial, but it helps me deal with the fact that if I aimed to leave with only 5 minutes I'd probably space out & be late.
